summary:
AstroGuard is an interactive health monitoring software designed for astronauts on long-duration space missions, such as lunar and Mars expeditions. We developed a visual digital twin application featuring an interactive body and cardiovascular system model that allows astronauts to track critical indicators like heart rate, blood pressure, hydration, and sleep.
The software addresses the challenge by providing clear, color-coded status indicators (normal, warning, critical risk) across key body systems, helping crew members instantly evaluate their physical state. It also delivers immediate, automated action protocols when parameters deviate, ensuring autonomous decision-making during deep-space communication delays.
This project is vital because long-duration spaceflight exposes crews to severe hazards—including microgravity fluid shifts, space radiation, and isolation—that strain the cardiovascular and immune systems. Empowering astronauts with an intuitive self-assessment tool bridges the communication gap with Earth, prevents critical health events, and safeguards crew well-being.
details:
AstroGuard is an interactive web-based digital twin application designed to monitor astronaut health during long-duration space missions, such as lunar and Mars expeditions.

How it works: The platform features an interactive visual model of the human body with a special focus on the cardiovascular system and blood vessels. Astronauts can click on key organs and systems to view real-time status indicators color-coded for safety (green for normal, yellow for warning, red for critical risk). A dynamic control panel allows users to adjust key indicators like blood pressure, heart rate, hydration, and sleep, immediately updating the visual model and triggering instant, automated action protocols for self-care during communication delays.

Benefits & Impact: It empowers crew members to independently track and evaluate physiological stresses—such as microgravity fluid shifts, cardiovascular strain, and isolation effects—bridging the communication gap with Earth and preventing critical health events.

Tools & Technologies: Built using HTML5, Tailwind CSS, and JavaScript. Super Intelligence (SI) tools (Claude Plus) were utilized to accelerate web prototyping, UI design, and code generation.

Creativity & Factors Considered: We prioritized an intuitive, low-friction UI tailored to the 5 key spaceflight hazards defined by NASA’s Human Research Program (radiation, isolation, altered gravity, distance, and hostile environments), focusing heavily on vascular and fluid health.
